section_2_the_question.heading: What does your brand feel like?
section_2_the_question.subtitle: Six intimate questions that define the difference between a place and a destination.

questions.title: 01 / NOTICE
questions.text: What do people notice in the first three seconds before they look at a price tag?

questions.title: 02 / FEEL
questions.text: What emotion hangs in the air when the door opens and the room quietens?

questions.title: 03 / DO
questions.text: How do guests instinctively move through your room without needing signs or prompts?

questions.title: 04 / REMEMBER
questions.text: Which lingering sensory trace remains in their mind three days after leaving?

questions.title: 05 / STAY
questions.text: What makes someone lose track of time and decide to stay for one more drink or chapter?

questions.title: 06 / COME BACK
questions.text: What subtle ritual forces them to return, bring a friend, and say 'you have to see this'?

section_3_what_i_do.title: WHAT I ACTUALLY DO
section_3_what_i_do.heading: I TURN BRAND WORLDS INTO EXPERIENCES PEOPLE CAN ENTER.

dimensions.name: SPACE
dimensions.desc: Volumetric flow, light direction, architectural intimacy, shadow play.

dimensions.name: SENSES
dimensions.desc: Bespoke olfactory signatures, tactile fabric curation, acoustic warmth.

dimensions.name: ATMOSPHERE
dimensions.desc: The invisible tension that gives a room its pulse, drama, and character.

dimensions.name: JOURNEY
dimensions.desc: Choreographed physical guest touchpoints from threshold to departure.

dimensions.name: INTERACTION
dimensions.desc: Human-to-human micro-rituals that turn transactions into hospitality.

dimensions.name: MEMORY
dimensions.desc: Tactile keepsakes, lingering scents, and emotional anchors.

section_3_what_i_do.closing: The experience people want to come back to.

section_4_how_i_work.title: HOW I WORK
section_4_how_i_work.subtitle: Three clear progressive stages. You don't need all three — enter where your brand is.

services.name: THE VIBE AUDIT
services.desc: An unannounced, deep-dive sensory walkthrough of your existing physical space or planned blueprints. Uncovering friction points, sensory disconnects, and missed emotional opportunities.

services.name: THE VIBE BLUEPRINT
services.desc: Translating brand DNA into a comprehensive sensory masterplan: lighting maps, material palettes, scent profiles, playlist direction, guest choreography, and staff interaction guides.

services.name: EXPERIENCE DESIGN
services.desc: Full creative direction and hands-on spatial execution. Working side-by-side with architects, interior fabricators, artisans, and staff to bring the physical world to life.

section_5_evidence.title: HOW DO YOU KNOW IT WORKS?
section_5_evidence.question: But how do you know?

layers.title: What people DO
layers.desc: Slower dwell times, instinctive phone-down presence, organic touch of surfaces.

layers.title: What people EXPERIENCE
layers.desc: A shift in mood, unprompted sighs of ease, genuine physical delight.

layers.title: What the brand INTENDS
layers.desc: Pure alignment between inner core philosophy and outer spatial reality.

layers.title: Where they MEET
layers.desc: The sweet spot where spatial design becomes unshakeable brand loyalty.

section_5_evidence.closing_statement: I don't measure 'vibe' with meaningless corporate surveys. I define concrete spatial and sensory signals that manifest in guest behavior.

section_6_vibe_studies.title: VIBE STUDIES
section_6_vibe_studies.subtitle: Speculative independent conceptual exploratory studies for world-class spaces.

studies.title: THE PERFUMER'S SANCTUARY
studies.concept: A darkened, sound-dampened velvet chamber where scents are experienced via warm vapor columns in sync with atmospheric lighting.

studies.title: LATE NIGHT AT THE DRAMATIST
studies.concept: An underground secret speakeasy lounge hidden behind vintage stage curtains, featuring ambient warmth, brass detailing, and curated whispers.

studies.title: THE ARCHIVE BOOKSHOP
studies.concept: A high-ceilinged literary haven with dark mahogany shelves, warm reading alcoves, and bespoke tea aromas.

section_7_how_i_see.heading: I NOTICE WHAT OTHERS MISS.
section_7_how_i_see.quote: A room is never neutral. Every light reflection, texture contrast, and acoustic reverberation is either telling your story or eroding it.

section_8_virginia.title: THE PERSON BEHIND THE VIBE
section_8_virginia.name: Virginia Cesarini
section_8_virginia.bio: I have spent my life obsessing over why certain places make us feel transformed while others feel instantly forgettable. Combining background in theatrical spatial design, luxury brand strategy, and sensory psychology, I founded THE VIBE CURATOR to give visionary brands a tangible physical soul.

frontend: Use React JS with Tailwind CSS, Framer Motion, Lenis for smooth scrolling, and Sonner for toasts.
Import Google Fonts 'Limelight', 'Cormorant Garamond', and 'Plus Jakarta Sans' in index.html / index.css.
Apply deep burgundy background (#24070A and #3B0C11) with rich gold accents (#C5A059) and warm cream typography (#FDFBF7).
Ensure all key interactive elements and sections contain explicit data-testid attributes (e.g. data-testid='hero-section', data-testid='contact-submit-button', data-testid='conversational-form').
Implement the Lenis smooth scroll engine for momentum scrolling throughout the site.
Build the conversational multi-step contact form that POSTs to /api/contact and displays the exact requested confirmation message on success.
Create slow editorial marquee using Framer Motion or react-fast-marquee.
backend: Ensure FastAPI backend has a POST /api/contact endpoint that accepts JSON body {name, sector, vision, email}.
Return JSON response with success status and confirmation message.

UNIVERSAL GUIDELINES FOR MAIN AGENT: You tend to converge toward generic, 'on distribution' outputs. In frontend design, this creates what users call the 'AI slop' aesthetic. Avoid this: make creative, distinctive frontends that surprise and delight.
Dark colors look good when used independently without gradients. DO NOT use dark colors as gradients.
Don't make generic centered layouts, simplistic gradients, and uniform styling.
Create depth through layered design elements with z-index hierarchy.
Use glass-morphism effects with backdrop filters (12-24px blur).
You MUST NOT apply universal transition. Eg: transition: all. This results in breaking transforms. Always add transitions for specific interactive elements like button, input excluding transforms.
You MUST NOT center align the app container, ie do not add .App { text-align: center; } in the css file. This disrupts the human natural reading flow of text.
Always use modern button styles like pill-shaped, or sharp button with interaction animations & color relevant to the app style.
NEVER: use AI assistant Emoji characters like 🤖🧠💭💡🔮🎯 etc for icons.
Every interaction needs micro-animations - hover states, transitions, parallax effects, and entrance animations. Static = dead.
Use 2-3x more spacing than feels comfortable. Cramped designs look cheap.
Subtle grain textures, noise overlays, custom cursors, selection states, and loading animations: separates good from extraordinary.
Main agent relies on these image URLs. Missing categories (especially sponsor logos) = main agent will use placeholder text which is FORBIDDEN.
Prioritize using pre-existing components from src/components/ui when applicable.
Create new components that match the style and conventions of existing components when needed.
Examine existing components to understand the project's component patterns before creating new ones.
Use sonner for toasts located in /app/src/components/ui/sonner.tsx or equivalent.
